title: Feature/2013 edit items in place
summary: Before, clicking an item in the playlist editor only highlighted it and showed a preview, while the form to change it sat in the **Add item** box at the bottom of the list. In reading plans, a separate pencil button did the same. Now clicking an item (or a reading) opens its editor right inside that item's row, pushing the rest of the list down. For scripture items the passage shows inside the editor. Only one item is open at a time, and if the open item has unsaved changes the app asks before closing it. Playlist rows now also get the same down/up arrow (caret) that reading plan rows have.

links.label: Issue 2013: Edit playlist and reading plan items in place, not in a form at the bottom of the list

setup.title: Open the preview on a computer
setup.body: Use the **Open the preview build** link above in Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari on a computer. If the page shows an error or doesn't load, the build may still be deploying: wait a few minutes and reload.

setup.title: Make sure you have the newest version
setup.body: The app saves a copy of itself in your browser, so it can show an older version. Do a hard refresh once the page has loaded: **Ctrl+Shift+R** on Windows, or **Cmd+Shift+R** on Mac. A private/incognito window gives you a clean start if anything looks odd.

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Sign in with your email address. You'll get a code by email, so use an inbox you can check. You need to be signed in to create playlists and reading plans.

setup.title: Build a test playlist
setup.body: Open the **Discover** pane, click **+ Create**, then **Playlist**. Type `Edit in place` as the title. In the **Add item** box at the bottom, use the **Item type** dropdown and click **Add item** after each of these, in this order: (1) **Scripture** `John 3`; (2) **Text** with title `Welcome` and text `Hello there.`; (3) **Link** `https://example.com`; (4) **Scripture** `Psalm 23`; (5) **Text** with title `Last note` and text `The end.` Leave the editor open.

tests.title: Each playlist row has an open/closed arrow
tests.why: Playlist rows now get the same caret as reading plan rows.
steps: Look at the five items in the list, without clicking any.
expected: Each row ends with a small arrow pointing **down** (before the trash/remove button).
No editor is showing under any of the items.

tests.title: Clicking a scripture item opens its editor right under it
tests.why: The main change: the editor opens at the item, not in the box at the bottom.
steps: Click the **John 3** row.
expected: A form opens directly under the **John 3** row, inside the list, pushing **Welcome** and the other items down.
The form has the reference box filled in with **John 3**, a **Save changes** button, the passage text of John 3 underneath, and a **Cancel** button.
The **John 3** row's arrow now points **up**.
The **Add item** box at the bottom of the list is unchanged: it still has the **Item type** dropdown and is empty.

tests.title: Changing a scripture item and saving closes it
tests.before: **John 3** is open from the last test.
steps: In the open editor, change the reference to `John 3:16`.
Click **Save changes**.
expected: The editor closes and the row now reads **John 3:16**, with its arrow pointing down.
The item stays in first place in the list.

tests.title: A bad reference shows an error and keeps the item open
steps: Click the **John 3:16** row.
Change the reference to `Notabook 99`.
Click **Save changes**.
expected: The message **Couldn't find that reference** appears and the editor stays open.
Click **Cancel**: the editor closes and the row still reads **John 3:16**.

tests.title: A text item can be edited where it is
steps: Click the **Welcome** row.
Change the title to `Welcome back`.
Click **Save changes**.
expected: The editor opened under **Welcome** showing its title and text (`Hello there.`), with no passage preview.
After saving, the editor closes and the row reads **Welcome back**.

tests.title: A link item can be edited where it is
steps: Click the **example.com** link row.
Type `Example site` in the **Title (optional)** box.
Click **Save changes**.
expected: The editor opened under the link row with `https://example.com` already filled in.
After saving, the editor closes and the row reads **Example site**.

tests.title: Cancel closes the item without keeping changes
steps: Click the **Last note** row.
Change the title to `Changed my mind`.
Click **Cancel**.
expected: The editor closes without asking anything, and the row still reads **Last note**.

tests.title: Clicking an open item's row again closes it
steps: Click the **Psalm 23** row to open it.
Without changing anything, click the **Psalm 23** row (the label, not the editor) again.
expected: The editor closes and the arrow points down again. No question pops up.

tests.title: Only one item is open at a time
steps: Click the **Psalm 23** row to open it.
Without changing anything, click the **Welcome back** row.
expected: The **Psalm 23** editor closes and the **Welcome back** editor opens. Only one editor shows in the list.
No question pops up, because nothing was changed.

tests.title: Switching away from unsaved changes asks first: Back
tests.why: New in this change: the app asks before throwing away edits when another item is opened.
steps: With **Welcome back** open, change its title to `Draft title`.
Click the **Psalm 23** row.
In the box that appears, click **Back**.
expected: A box titled **Unsaved item changes** appears saying **You've changed this item but haven't saved those changes yet. What would you like to do?**, with **Back**, **Discard changes** and **Save changes** buttons.
After **Back**, the box closes, **Welcome back** is still open with `Draft title` still typed in, and **Psalm 23** is not open.

tests.title: Switching away from unsaved changes: Discard changes
tests.before: **Welcome back** is open with `Draft title` typed in, from the last test.
steps: Click the **Psalm 23** row.
Click **Discard changes**.
expected: **Psalm 23** opens and **Welcome back** closes.
The row still reads **Welcome back**: the `Draft title` change was thrown away.

tests.title: Switching away from unsaved changes: Save changes
steps: Click the **Welcome back** row and change its title to `Saved by the prompt`.
Click the **Last note** row.
Click **Save changes** in the box that appears.
expected: The box closes, **Last note** opens, and the other row now reads **Saved by the prompt**.

tests.title: Saving through the prompt with a bad reference keeps you on the item
steps: Click the **Psalm 23** row and change its reference to `Notabook 99`.
Click the **Saved by the prompt** row.
Click **Save changes** in the box that appears.
expected: The box closes, **Psalm 23**'s editor stays open with **Couldn't find that reference**, and **Saved by the prompt** does not open.
Click **Cancel** to close it; the row still reads **Psalm 23**.

tests.title: Saving the playlist with an open, changed item asks first
steps: Click the **Last note** row and change its title to `Final words`.
Without clicking **Save changes** in the item, click the playlist's own **Save** (or **Save & exit**) button at the bottom.
Choose **Keep changes and save**.
expected: A box titled **Unsaved item changes** appears with **Back**, **Discard and save** and **Keep changes and save**.
After **Keep changes and save**, the playlist saves. Open it again with **Edit playlist** (from its ⋮ options menu in Discover): the item reads **Final words**.

tests.title: A half-typed new item still asks before saving
tests.why: The **Add item** box kept its old warning; this checks it still works next to the new in-row editor.
tests.before: The playlist editor for `Edit in place` is open, with no item open.
steps: In the **Add item** box at the bottom, choose **Scripture** and type `Romans 8`, but don't click **Add item**.
Click the playlist's **Save** button.
Choose **Add and save**.
expected: A box titled **Unsaved item** appears, saying you've started adding an item that hasn't been added yet, with **Back**, **Discard and save** and **Add and save**.
After **Add and save**, the playlist saves, and reopening it shows **Romans 8** at the end of the list.

tests.title: The open item follows a drag or a removal
tests.before: The playlist editor for `Edit in place` is open.
steps: Click the **Psalm 23** row to open it.
Drag the **John 3:16** row (by its ⋮⋮ handle on the left) down below **Psalm 23**.
Then click the trash/remove button on a row **above** the open one.
expected: After the drag, **Psalm 23**'s editor is still the one that's open (not some other item).
After removing the other row, **Psalm 23** is still the one open.
Finally, remove **Psalm 23** itself: its editor disappears with it and nothing else opens. Leave without saving if you don't want to keep these changes.

sections.title: Editing reading plan readings in place

setup.title: Start a test reading plan
setup.body: Open **Reading plans** and click **Create reading plan**. Name it `Edit in place plan` and continue to **Select readings**. In **Session 1**, add **Scripture** `Psalm 1` and **Text** with title `Intro` and text `Read slowly.` Click **Add session**, and in **Session 2** add **Scripture** `Psalm 2`. Stay on this screen.

tests.title: There is no pencil (edit) button on readings any more
tests.why: The issue asks to drop the separate pencil button: clicking the reading opens it for editing.
steps: Look at the **Psalm 1** reading row.
expected: The row has the reading's name, a down arrow, and an **X** (remove) button. There is no pencil button.

tests.title: Clicking a reading opens its editor inside the row
steps: Click the **Psalm 1** row.
expected: An editor opens inside the **Psalm 1** row, with the reference box filled in, a **Save changes** button, the passage text of Psalm 1, and **Cancel**.
The row's border is highlighted and its arrow points up.
Session 1's own add-reading box (with the **Item type** dropdown) is still there below the readings, empty.

tests.title: Editing and saving a reading closes it
steps: Change the reference to `Psalm 1:1-3`.
Click **Save changes**.
expected: The editor closes and the row now reads **Psalm 1:1-3**.

tests.title: Only one reading is open at a time, across sessions
steps: Click the **Intro** reading in Session 1.
Without changing anything, click **Psalm 2** in Session 2.
expected: **Intro** closes and **Psalm 2** opens inside Session 2. Only one reading editor shows on the screen.
No question pops up, because nothing was changed.

tests.title: Switching readings with unsaved changes asks first
steps: With **Psalm 2** open, change the reference to `Psalm 3`.
Click the **Intro** reading.
Click **Save changes** in the box that appears.
expected: A box titled **Unsaved item changes** appears with **Back**, **Discard changes** and **Save changes**.
After **Save changes**, Session 2's reading reads **Psalm 3**, and **Intro** is now open.

tests.title: Saving the plan with an open, changed reading asks first
steps: With **Intro** open, change its title to `Introduction`.
Without clicking **Save changes** inside the reading, scroll to the bottom of the editor and click **Create plan**.
Choose **Keep changes and save**.
expected: A box titled **Unsaved item changes** appears with **Back**, **Discard and save** and **Keep changes and save**.
After **Keep changes and save**, the plan saves. Open it with **Edit plan** from its ⋮ menu: the reading reads **Introduction**.

tests.title: Editing a saved plan works the same way
tests.before: `Edit in place plan` was created in the last test.
steps: Open the plan's ⋮ menu and choose **Edit plan**, then go to the readings.
Click **Psalm 3**, change it to `Psalm 4`, click **Save changes** in the reading, then save the plan.
expected: The editor opens in the reading's row just as when creating, and after saving the plan shows **Psalm 4** in Session 2.

setup.title: Make the window narrow
setup.body: Open the preview on a phone (and sign in there), or make your browser window very narrow, about the width of a phone. Open **Edit playlist** on `Edit in place` from its ⋮ menu in Discover.

tests.title: The in-row editor fits on a narrow screen
steps: Tap a scripture item to open it.
Scroll left and right inside the list.
expected: The editor takes the full width under the row. The reference box, **Save changes**, the passage and **Cancel** all fit without the page scrolling sideways.
The drag handle, label, arrow and remove button of the row stay on one line above the editor.

tests.title: The in-row editor is readable in dark mode
steps: Switch the app to dark mode (in settings, under Display & Theme).
Open an item in the playlist editor and a reading in the reading plan editor.
expected: Text, boxes, the arrow and the highlighted border of the open reading are all clearly visible against the dark background.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: Adding items with the Add item box still works
steps: In a playlist editor, add a **Text** item through the **Add item** box at the bottom.
In a reading plan editor, click a session and add a **Link** reading through its add box.
expected: Both new items appear at the end of their list, and the add box clears for the next one.

tests.title: Leaving the playlist editor with an open, changed item still warns
steps: In the playlist editor, open an item and change it without saving.
Click the editor's **Cancel** button at the bottom (the one for the whole playlist, not the item's).
expected: A box titled **Unsaved changes** says you have unsaved changes and offers **Confirm**, **Go back** and **Save & exit**, instead of closing straight away. Click **Go back** to stay.

tests.title: Playing the edited playlist shows the edited items
steps: In Discover, click the round **Play playlist** button (▶) on `Edit in place`.
Step through items with **Next** in the bottom toolbar.
expected: Each item plays with its edited name and content (for example, the text item shows its new title). Click **Stop** when done.

notCovered: Translation files other than English: this PR also reorders and de-duplicates entries in the English text file, which has no visible effect.
Screen reader labels (the reading row is now announced as **Edit** plus the reading's name instead of **Preview**): these are covered by unit tests.
